title: Narrated explainer video
summary: A collection of nouns and verbs for making a narrated explainer video with code, every step a claimed verb that ends with a receipt: a script and a cut plan on one frame clock, narration placed on its beats, scenes rendered from a frame-addressable HTML stage, captions timed to the measured voice and checked against what it said, a caption-free master and an open-captions variant, video checks and a frame sheet, a ledger of every receipt, and a release manifest that hashes every delivered file before the owner decides.
boundaries: Every step is a claimed verb that submits once with an execution report; failed attempts stay on the record.
Scenes are code rendered by a pinned browser build; no model draws a frame.
Workers never release the video; the owner decides and records it.
Importing the pack writes nothing, enqueues nothing and installs no code.

nouns.title: Frame clock rules for a cut plan
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same inputs always give the same result.

rules: A clip starts where the previous clip ends minus its crossfade frames; the first clip starts at frame 0 with no crossfade, and a crossfade is no longer than either clip it joins.

A beat runs from the middle of the crossfade into its first clip to the middle of the crossfade into the next beat's first clip; the first beat starts at 0 and the last ends with the cut. A beat is one run of clips.
A cut's clips add up to its duration times its fps exactly.
A narration line starts inside its beat, at least 0.2 s after the previous line ends, and ends at least 0.1 s before the cut ends.
A frame-sheet frame for a clip is taken at the middle of the span where it plays alone: from the end of its crossfade in to the start of the next clip.
Times are whole milliseconds and frames are integers; a time between frames rounds to the nearest frame, halves up.

nouns.title: Rules for scenes rendered from a frame-addressable HTML stage
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same inputs always give the same result.

value.contract: The stage page exposes boot(scene, config), which builds a scene, and renderFrame(t), which draws scene time t in seconds.
rules: Every visible property is a pure function of scene time t: no clock reads, no CSS animations or transitions, no timers and no unseeded randomness, so any frame can be rendered in any order.
Fonts are embedded from pinned files with their licenses and checked as loaded before the first frame; every image is a local file pinned by digest and checked as loaded.
The stage loads nothing from the network while rendering.

Frames render at 1920 by 1080 and device scale 1 with the pinned headless browser build and the flags --force-color-profile=srgb and --disable-gpu; frame i of a slice is drawn at t equal to its start plus i over fps.
Each slice is encoded losslessly with libx264rgb at qp 0 with bit-exact flags, so composing works on exact frames.
Determinism is checked, not assumed: sampled frames rendered shuffled and repeated must match the in-order pixel digests.
Pixel identity holds only for the same browser build, fonts and flags; record all three.

nouns.title: Caption rules: text from the script, timing from the measured voice
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same inputs always give the same result.

value.numbers_from: The video showcase style guide's caption rules: at most 2 lines of 42 characters, 1 to 7 s on screen and at most 17 characters per second. They are stricter than the render tools' own minimums, so cues that pass here pass there.
steps: Cue text comes from the placed narration lines, never from speech recognition.
Split each line at sentence ends; split a sentence longer than 80 characters, or one that two lines cannot hold, at the comma nearest its middle, and at the middle word when it has no comma.
Place each split at the unused measured pause nearest a character-proportional estimate when one lies within 1.2 s; otherwise at the estimate.
End each cue 0.25 s after its speech, or later when its text needs more time at 16.4 characters per second; never past the next cue's start or 7 s, and the last cue 0.05 s before the cut ends.
Snap starts and ends to frames, halves up, and close any gap of 1 or 2 frames by ending the earlier cue where the next begins.
Wrap each cue into one line, or two lines as even as the words allow.
Write WebVTT and SRT sidecars from the same cues; burn captions only into the open-captions variant.
Check what the voice said with a pinned local recognizer: a line over the error-rate limit, 0.06 by default, is listed as a deviation and never silently fixed.
